newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hart happy with 19.9 pct Burns stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hart happy with 19.9 pct Burns stake - paper.

text.p: New Zealand investor Graeme Hart has said he was behind the purchase late on Wednesday of a further 3.5 percent of troubled food group Burns Philp & Co Ltd, the Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Thursday.
Hart bought 14.9 percent of Burns Philp earlier this month and is now the largest shareholder in the Sydney-based group.
The Financial Review reported that Hart intended to go to the 19.9 percent threshold, but remained coy about his intentions for Burns Philp.
Hart needs approval from Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) to lift his stake to 19.9 percent.
"Our intention hasn't changed, we wanted 19.9 percent," Hart was quoted as saying to the newspaper.

The paper reported that it asked Hart if he planned to make a takeover offer for Burns Philp and it quoted the New Zealand businessman as saying :"I'm not going to answer that. We're quite happy where we are at this stage."
After Wednesday's close of trade, brokers Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) bought about 19 million Burns Philp shares at A$2.50 per share, paying a total of about A$47.5 million.
The Finanial Review reported that DMG was holding the shares in principal until Hart gains FIRB approval.
Hart and DMG had an equity swap arrangement in place for an additional five percent stake in Burns Philp, on top of the 14.9 percent he owns through his unlisted Rank Group.
Burns Philp shares closed one cent down at A$2.37 with 19.3 million shares traded.
Almost a million Burns Philp shares were traded before Thursday's market open.

Brokers have said A$2.50 is a top price to pay for Burns Philp, which is planning to sell its herbs and spice businesses to focus on its yeast business, while at the same time it is involved in ongoing litigation over the Estate Mortgage Trusts.
Estate Mortgage, for which a Burns Philp subsidiary was trustee, collapsed in 1990 with A$600 million in losses.
